title: Consolidate sampled tail latency metrics and enrich console traces after capacity regression
creator: Maya Chen
description: Follow-up from 2026-03-09 capacity regression that caused elevated tail latencies for a subset of dedicated tenants. Investigation showed multiple blind spots in console telemetry: heavy sampling that suppressed tail signals, dashboards aggregating across tenants which hid per-tenant spikes, and missing trace context linking Console UI requests to runtime shards and KV cache hits. This ticket consolidates the findings and tracks remediation: add per-tenant histograms, increase / adapt sampling for tail-sensitive metrics, enrich traces with Console->runtime correlation IDs, and add synthetic/alerting coverage for identified failure modes.
timeline: 2026-03-09 02:14 UTC: Automated SLO alert triggered for client-facing latency (SLO breach for 3 tenants).
2026-03-09 02:30 UTC: Ops paged on partial P95/P99 mismatch between runtime logs and Console dashboards.
2026-03-09 03:05 UTC: War room formed; initial mitigation: increase autoscale buffer for Dedicated pools.
2026-03-09 07:20 UTC: Runtime team identified KV-cache eviction storms correlated with higher per-token CPU and latency.
2026-03-10 11:00 UTC: Small triage) discovered console dashboards used sampled percentile aggregates and a tenant-aggregation layer which hid tail values.
2026-03-11 15:45 UTC: Confirmed tracing pipeline dropped console correlation-id at ingest; unable to join UI request to runtime spans.
findings: Metric sampling: global 1% sampling on latency histograms suppressed intermittent P99 signals from heavy tenants.
Aggregation blind spot: console dashboards compute percentiles after aggregating many tenants, masking tenant-level tails.
Missing per-tenant KV-cache metrics: cache hit/eviction rates are only visible at cluster level, not per-tenant, preventing targeted diagnosis.
Tracing gap: Console frontend request IDs are not propagated into the runtime trace pipeline due to a header strip in the edge proxy.
Synthetic coverage gap: no synthetic checks exercising the long-sequence generation path where KV-cache cold starts occur.
action_items: AL-1: Add per-tenant latency histograms (p50/p95/p99) to the telemetry pipeline and store aggregated+raw buckets for 7d — owner: Arjun Patel — estimate: 3 — due: 2026-03-24
AL-2: Implement adaptive sampling: keep full-resolution samples for requests that exceed dynamic latency thresholds (preserve tail events) — owner: Priya Rao — estimate: 5 — due: 2026-03-28

AL-3: Emit per-tenant KV-cache metrics (hit/miss/eviction, cold-start counters) from runtime with tenant_id tag and wire through the console metrics ingestion — owner: Linus Becker — estimate: 3 — due: 2026-03-26

AL-4: Fix edge proxy header stripping so Console correlation-id header is preserved; update tracing middleware to attach correlation-id to runtime spans — owner: Arjun Patel — estimate: 2 — due: 2026-03-18

AL-5: Create a Console->Runtime join dashboard that surfaces per-tenant latency, KV-cache activity, and trace links for quick RCA — owner: Data Viz Team (review by Maya Chen) — estimate: 3 — due: 2026-03-30

AL-6: Add synthetic test suite covering long-sequence generation and cache-warmup behavior; wire results into alerting and weekly regression jobs — owner: QA Automation — estimate: 4 — due: 2026-04-05
AL-7: Add alerts for sudden divergence between cluster and per-tenant percentiles and for increasing cache-eviction rates — owner: SRE/Oncall — estimate: 2 — due: 2026-03-21
